title: Surely I Am Coming Soon
summary: Jesus says three times that he is coming soon. Longing for his return gives us joy, and it sends us out with the gospel to those we love.
exhortation: In the last chapter of the Bible, Jesus says three times that he is coming soon. "Behold, I am coming soon. Blessed is the one who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book." Again, "Behold, I am coming soon, bringing my recompense with me, to repay each one for what he has done." And again, "Surely I am coming soon." Amen. Come, Lord Jesus.

We see that when Jesus returns, it will be a blessing for those who are found in him. It will be our greatest joy realized. And yet we also see that when Jesus returns, it will be a terror, a judgment, for those who are not in him.

There's a tension when we long for the return of Jesus. Many times, as I'm praying or just thinking, "Lord, come quickly," my very next thought is of the people I love who are not in Christ. Elsewhere the Bible makes clear that it's the patience and the grace of God that he delays his coming. And yet he says, "I am coming soon." So there's a tension as we long to see Jesus face to face, to see a sinful world judged, and to see every tear wiped away.

I think it's good for us as Christians to meditate on this and to long for it, because it reminds us of our mission here. It reminds us that nothing is wasted, that Jesus is coming back, and that he will right every wrong. But it also reminds us to be bold with the gospel and to pray for those we love, that they would come to saving faith in Jesus. What a wonderful promise we have in the very last chapter of the Bible. Jesus reminds us again and again and again that he is coming soon. And together we say, amen. Come, Lord Jesus.
prayer: Lord, help us to long for you with eager expectation. Help our unbelief where there is unbelief. Where there is doubting, help us to trust you fully. Help us to read your word, to read Revelation 22, with a believing, longing heart that knows you will do what you said you will do. You will come. You will return soon, and we don't want to be caught unready. So may we wait for you, Lord, with eager expectation and with joy. Amen.
